enonce.texte:
Read the sentences below and identify the function of each modal verb. Choose from: Obligation, Necessity, Prohibition, Permission, Ability, or Possibility.

  • You must wear a seatbelt in the car.
  • Students may leave the classroom after the bell rings.
  • She can speak three languages fluently.
  • You must not smoke in this building.
  • We should arrive by noon if we leave now.
  • He could be at the office; I'm not sure.
images: A collage of everyday situations: a person buckling a seatbelt, a student leaving a classroom, a multilingual person talking, a no-smoking sign, a clock showing noon, and a person looking at an office building.

questions.texte: Identify the function of each modal verb in the sentences provided.
questions.reponse: 1. Obligation, 2. Permission, 3. Ability, 4. Prohibition, 5. Possibility/Assumption, 6. Possibility

sousQuestions.texte: Explain the difference between 'must' and 'may' in terms of function.
sousQuestions.reponse: 'Must' expresses obligation or a rule that must be followed. 'May' expresses permission or a possibility, indicating that something is allowed to happen.

intitule: Resource: Degrees of Certainty with Modals

enonce.texte:
Analyze the following situations and choose the correct modal verb to express the appropriate degree of certainty. The options are: must, might, could, can't, may.

  • The lights are on in her office. She ______ be working late.
  • He said he would be here at 6, and he's never late. He ______ be stuck in traffic, but it's unlikely.
  • The weather forecast said it would rain, but the sky is clear. It ______ rain later today.
  • She has a Ph.D. in Physics. She ______ understand quantum mechanics easily.
  • You haven't eaten all day. You ______ be hungry.
images: A diagram showing a scale of certainty from 0% to 100%, with modals placed on the scale (can't = 0%, might/could = 50%, may = 60%, must = 95%).

questions.texte: Fill in the blanks with the most appropriate modal verb to express the degree of certainty.

sousQuestions.texte: Rewrite sentence 2 to express the opposite meaning (that he is definitely not stuck in traffic).
sousQuestions.reponse: He can't be stuck in traffic because he is never late and always arrives on time.

enonce.texte:
Read the following scenarios. For each one, write two sentences: one expressing regret about a past action and another expressing criticism about a past decision or failure. Use perfect modals ($should have$, $could have$, $must have$).

  • Scenario A: You missed a friend's wedding because your flight was delayed.
  • Scenario B: A colleague's project failed because they didn't consult the team.
images: A picture of an airport with delayed flight signs, and a picture of a team meeting with a disappointed manager.

questions.texte: Write two sentences for each scenario: one for regret and one for criticism.
questions.reponse: Scenario A: Regret: I should have booked an earlier flight to avoid the delay. Criticism: The airline could have informed us about the delay earlier. Scenario B: Regret: The team should have been consulted before the project started. Criticism: The manager must have overlooked the importance of team input.

sousQuestions.texte: Explain the difference in meaning between 'should have' and 'could have' in your sentences.
sousQuestions.reponse: 'Should have' expresses a missed obligation or a better choice that was not made. 'Could have' expresses a missed opportunity or possibility that was available but not taken.

intitule: Competence: Applying Modals in a Professional Context

enonce.texte:
You are the manager of a company. You need to write a memo to your team about a new policy regarding remote work. The memo must include:

  • An obligation for all employees to attend a mandatory virtual meeting.
  • Permission for employees to work from home on Fridays.
  • Necessity for employees to submit a weekly progress report.
  • Prohibition against using company devices for personal purposes.
  • A suggestion for using a new project management tool.
  • A level of certainty that the policy will improve productivity.
images: A formal office memo template with a company logo and sections for 'To', 'From', 'Date', and 'Subject'.

questions.texte: Write the full memo. Include at least one example of each type of modal function mentioned in the scenario.
questions.reponse:
Subject: New Remote Work Policy

Dear Team,

I am writing to announce our new remote work policy, effective next month. 

All employees must attend a mandatory virtual meeting this Friday at 10 AM to discuss the details. You may work from home on Fridays, provided you have completed all your tasks for the week. However, you must not use company devices for personal purposes at any time. 

It is necessary that each employee submits a weekly progress report every Thursday evening. Additionally, I suggest using the new project management tool, Trello, to track your tasks. 

With these changes, the company should see an improvement in productivity and employee satisfaction. I believe this policy will positively impact our workflow.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

sousQuestions.texte: Justify the use of each modal verb in your memo and explain the effect on the reader.
sousQuestions.reponse: 'Must attend' creates a clear obligation, ensuring attendance. 'May work' gives permission, making the policy flexible. 'Must not use' creates a strict prohibition, protecting company assets. 'Is necessary' emphasizes the importance of the report. 'Suggest' offers a recommendation without forcing, maintaining a positive tone. 'Should see' expresses confidence without overpromising.

intitule: Competence: Critical Analysis of Modal Use in a Speech

enonce.texte:
Read the following excerpt from a politician's speech. Identify and analyze the use of modal verbs, focusing on how they shape the message, express certainty, and influence the audience.

'We must act now to address climate change. We cannot afford to wait any longer. Every citizen should do their part to reduce carbon emissions. The government could implement new policies, but it must work with international partners. We might face severe consequences if we delay, but we can still turn things around if we commit to change.'
images: A picture of a politician speaking at a podium with a large audience.

questions.texte: Analyze the modal verbs used in the speech. Classify them by function and degree of certainty. Then, evaluate the overall impact of these modals on the message.
questions.reponse:
'Must act' - Obligation, high certainty; 'Cannot afford' - Prohibition/Necessity, high certainty; 'Should do' - Advice/Obligation, medium certainty; 'Could implement' - Possibility, low certainty; 'Must work' - Obligation, high certainty; 'Might face' - Possibility, low certainty; 'Can turn' - Ability/Possibility, medium certainty.

Impact: The speech uses strong obligation modals ('must', 'cannot') to create urgency. It balances this with softer modals ('could', 'might') to show flexibility and possibility. This mix makes the message compelling but not overly authoritarian. The overall effect is to persuade the audience that action is necessary and possible, while acknowledging the challenges.

sousQuestions.texte: Rewrite the speech using only high-certainty modals and analyze the effect.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Revised: 'We must act now. We cannot wait. Every citizen must do their part. The government must implement new policies and must work with international partners. We will face severe consequences if we delay, and we will turn things around if we commit to change.'

Effect: This version is much more forceful and prescriptive. It removes the element of choice and makes the outcomes seem inevitable. While it is more direct, it may come across as less collaborative and more authoritarian, potentially alienating some audience members.
